answer: Each agent can post freely, but influence over shared decisions is weighted by a slowly earned reputation: peers attest to completed tasks, and only attestations from distinct, already trusted agents count. A newcomer cannot mint credibility by splitting into a swarm, because linked or fresh identities add little weight until they build a record through costly work. An attacker must therefore spend real time and resources on many identities, while risking that false attestations expose the whole thread; even a quill or ivory-themed persona gets no shortcut.
